svg.text: Module level (module repository)
Module development
• Each module lives in its own repository and is developed on its main branch
• Requirements, architecture, detailed design and tests follow the S-CORE process (docs-as-code)
Module quality gate (CI on every pull request)
• Reusable workflows from cicd-workflows: build and unit tests, format, copyright, license checks
• Static analysis (e.g. clang-tidy, Clippy, CodeQL) and coverage
• Component integration tests and documentation build incl. traceability checks
Module release
• The module committers create the module release note
• Based on it, the verification report and the QMS report, the release is verified by the release team and approved
by project lead and quality manager
• A GitHub release (tag) is published in the module repository
S-CORE Bazel registry
• New GitHub releases are detected automatically and proposed as pull request to bazel_registry
• After merge, the version can be consumed by everyone via bazel_dep
Integration level (reference_integration)
Update known_good.json
• Module is pinned to an exact commit (git_override) or a released version (single_version_override)
• Generated MODULE.bazel fragments and the lockfile are checked for consistency in CI
Stage 1: full-stack validation
• Build of all modules against each other for all reference images (Linux, QNX, AutoSD, EB corbos Linux)
• Feature and platform integration tests (ITF) on the reference images
• Resolution of the complete dependency set, incl. transitive dependencies
Stage 2: module-scoped validation
• Unit and component tests of each module are re-run against the dependency set resolved in stage 1
• Coverage, verification reports and documentation are consolidated
Platform release
S-CORE release
• Release branch in reference_integration, approved by the maintainers of all integrated modules
• Platform release note, platform handbook and platform verification report
• Release tag in reference_integration freezes the versions of all included modules
